title: Blazing Fury — Fire Move Build
description: An Ember-to-Fire-Blast plan built around Power and careful spacing.
tips: Charizard and the listed Fire starters can learn Ember and Fire Spin from their Fire pool.
Take Power and concentrate upgrades on Ember to reach level 5, then choose Fire Blast.
After establishing damage, work toward Fire Spin plus Synthesis for Sacred Fire as close-range coverage.
A Rift Bond can join the learned attacks into one active slot. Do not assume independent slots fire together.

plan.when: Choose this when you want to focus on Ember first, with Fire Spin available as a second damage path.
plan.fallback: If Fire Spin does not appear, keep upgrading Ember. Quick Attack gives a separate Normal-type option; its evolution needs Sprint.
priorities: Finish Ember at level 5, then take Fire Blast.
Add Fire Spin + Synthesis if the cards allow it.

title: Tidal Momentum — Water Move Build
description: A Bubble-to-Surf plan with Sprint as its required card.
tips: The listed Water partners can learn Bubble even when their opening move is Water Gun.
Take Sprint and upgrade Bubble to level 5 for the Surf evolution.
A Water Gun path uses Power and evolves into Scald, so budget a separate evolution card.
Keep moving through open lanes; a second move is coverage to switch to until you obtain a Bond.

plan.when: Choose this for a Bubble evolution goal with Water Gun as a compatible alternative.
plan.fallback: If Bubble does not appear, develop Water Gun with Power toward Scald. Do not spend rerolls assuming Bubble is guaranteed.
priorities: Reach level 5 Bubble, then select Surf.
Use Water Gun + Power for another evolution route.

title: Returning Leaves — Grass Move Build
description: A Razor-Leaf-to-Leaf-Storm plan built around Reflexes.
tips: All listed Grass partners can learn Razor Leaf from their type pool.
Take Reflexes and upgrade Razor Leaf to level 5 to unlock Leaf Storm.
Vine Whip uses Power for Power Whip, offering a close-range alternative.
Practice spacing so returning attacks pass through approaching groups; the build is a strategy suggestion, not a DPS benchmark.

plan.when: Choose this to build around Razor Leaf and plan your positioning around its returning attacks.
plan.fallback: If Razor Leaf does not appear, Vine Whip + Power provides a compatible route to Power Whip. Tackle + Vigor is another available option.
priorities: Learn Razor Leaf and take Reflexes.
Reach level 5, then select Leaf Storm.
Build Vine Whip + Power for a close-range alternative.

title: Ghost Coverage — Gengar Build
description: A verified Ghost-pool plan: Shadow Ball with Reflexes, then Hex with Magnet.
tips: Gengar starts with Shadow Ball and can learn Hex and Lick from its Ghost pool.
Reach level 5 Shadow Ball and take Reflexes to unlock Phantom Force.
Hex needs Magnet and evolves into Poltergeist. Consider it after securing your first damage path.
Work toward a Rift Bond before expecting both attacks to operate together.

plan.when: Choose this when you want a Shadow Ball evolution first and can leave the second path until later.
plan.fallback: Stay with Shadow Ball if Hex is not offered. Lick is another Ghost-pool option; check its own evolution requirement before committing.
priorities: Level Shadow Ball and take Reflexes.
Consider Hex + Magnet after the core is ready.

title: Electric Perimeter — Pikachu Build
description: Thunder Shock → Thunder, backed by Discharge as an alternative close-range attack.
tips: Pikachu starts with Thunder Shock. Electric partners share the Electric move pool.
Use Power and level 5 Thunder Shock to unlock Thunder.
Discharge requires Armor for Electric Terrain; Thunderbolt requires Reflexes for Zap Cannon.
These are alternatives to prioritize as cards arrive, not three guaranteed simultaneous attacks.

plan.when: Choose this to start with Thunder Shock and keep Discharge or Thunderbolt as alternative card paths.
plan.fallback: If Power is delayed, continue improving Thunder Shock. Discharge needs Armor and Thunderbolt needs Reflexes; commit to the route your cards support.
priorities: Take Power and upgrade Thunder Shock.
Choose Discharge or Thunderbolt as follow-up coverage.

title: Psychic & Fairy — Gardevoir Build
description: A Psychic / Fairy coverage plan with Confusion, Dazzling Gleam and clear evolution cards.
tips: Ralts and Gardevoir can learn the listed Psychic and Fairy attacks.
Confusion needs Reflexes at level 5 to become Psyshock.
Dazzling Gleam needs Synthesis for Misty Terrain; Psybeam uses Power for Future Sight.
Secure one evolution first, then consider secondary coverage and a Bond. Choose a sustain item when attrition is the main problem.

plan.when: Choose this for a Confusion core with access to a Fairy alternative through Dazzling Gleam.
plan.fallback: If Dazzling Gleam is not offered, Psybeam + Power leads to Future Sight. Avoid splitting too many upgrades before the first evolution.
priorities: Consider Dazzling Gleam + Synthesis or Psybeam + Power.
